pages.title: Welcome
pages.subtitle: Most goals fail before they are written

blocks.heading: The problem is selection, not effort
paragraphs: People rarely abandon goals because they lacked discipline. They abandon goals they should never have chosen: goals set in an area of life that was already fine, goals that competed with three others, goals whose obvious risk was never named.

blocks.heading: So this planner starts before the goal
items: Score the twelve areas of your life and find the gap
Prioritise, so three goals survive and nine wait
Assess the risk to each one while you still have options
Align your habits to the goals they actually serve
Review weekly and monthly, on a fixed cadence

blocks.heading: What it is not
paragraphs: It is not a vision board and it will not tell you what to want. It gives you a scored picture of where you are, a method for choosing between competing goals, and a review rhythm that catches drift in weeks rather than quarters.

blocks.heading: The honest bit
paragraphs: The Weekly Review is the page that makes the rest work, and it is the page everyone skips. Twenty minutes, same day each week. If you will not do that, buy a notebook instead and save your money.

pages.title: Instructions
pages.subtitle: One evening to set up, twenty minutes a week to run

blocks.heading: Choose your size
paragraphs: Four sizes are included and all four contain identical pages. A4 and US Letter suit the desk. A5 and Half Letter suit a tablet or a bag, and print two-up on a full sheet.

blocks.heading: Set up once
items: Score all twelve life areas on the assessment page, honestly and quickly
Fill the gap analysis page for the three lowest scores
Write the vision, then draft more goals than you intend to keep
Run the Priority Matrix and cut to three
Write a SMART worksheet for each survivor
Assess the risk to each goal before writing a single action

blocks.heading: Every week
items: Weekly Review — twenty minutes, same day
Update the Progress Tracker and the habit alignment page
Set the coming week's goal actions

blocks.heading: Every month
items: Monthly Review — what the four weeks actually produced
Re-score any life area that has moved
One line on the Progress Dashboard

blocks.heading: Digital use
items: Import the PDF as a document, not as an image
Switch to read mode to tap links, write mode to write
Use the Review tab to reach the weekly review from any page

pages.title: Goal Setting Guide
pages.subtitle: Six rules, and the reasoning behind each

blocks.heading: Assess before you aspire
paragraphs: A goal set in an area already scoring eight out of ten produces small returns. The same effort in an area scoring three changes your life. Score first; choose second.

blocks.heading: Three goals, and the rest wait
paragraphs: Goals compete for the same finite evenings. Four goals do not run at eighty per cent each — two of them stall entirely while you feel busy. The Priority Matrix exists to make the cut deliberate rather than accidental.

blocks.heading: A goal without a number is a wish
items: Write the number and the date on the SMART page
Write where the number is today, not only where you want it
If you cannot measure it, measure the behaviour beneath it

blocks.heading: Name the risk while you still have options
paragraphs: Every goal has a foreseeable failure. Illness, a busy quarter at work, running out of money, losing interest in week six. Scored for likelihood and impact in advance, most of these have a cheap mitigation. Discovered in month three, they end the goal.

blocks.heading: Habits serve goals or they are hobbies
paragraphs: The Habit Alignment page asks which goal each habit feeds. Habits that serve nothing are fine — but they should not be counted as progress.

blocks.heading: Review weekly, not when you remember
paragraphs: Drift is invisible day to day and obvious across four weeks. A fixed weekly slot catches it early enough to correct; a review whenever you feel like it catches it in the post-mortem.
